title.narrative: LocaL 2030: Scaling local-level implementation and coalescing United Nations system collaboration to localize the Sustainable Development Goals

description.narrative:
Successful implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) requires unprecedented ownership by local actors, particularly city, state and regional governments, civil society leaders and private sector institutions.
Local2030 is a network that brings together the United Nations (UN) system, local actors, national, regional and local governments, the private sector, employers and worker organizations, civil society, academia, and other partners to pursue a common mission: to support and accelerate the implementation of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) at the local level. Building on a successful pilot phase, the UN-wide strategy outlined in this document will facilitate the global rollout of Local2030. Local2030 engaged in extensive efforts to establish the initiative as a key knowledge, solutions incubation, and advocacy platform for strengthened engagement between the United Nations and local governments; and local implementation of the SDGs. Local2030 moreover built an extensive global network that includes over 20 UN agencies and over 30 external partners. Eventually, Local2030 will comprise the entire UN system to advance system-wide collaboration on localization, with active advice from a strategic group of core UN agencies and departments that are focused on the local-level implementation and roll-out of the initiative. Local2030’s theory of change is based on the premise that collective action by such a global coalition of actors can mobilize the resources, knowledge, and partnerships needed to support effective SDG localization. Localization of the SDGs refers to efforts that support the achievement of the 2030 Agenda at the local level. To achieve this, local and regional governments will need to work closely with local actors such businesses and the private sector, neighbourhood associations, and civil society. Moreover, local and regional governments will ideally align their priorities, policies, and budgets with the SDGs in close cooperation with their respective national governments. Local2030 is committed to developing the initiative as a true bottom-up process, supporting local governments and other local actors in taking initiative to put their communities on a path towards greater sustainability, prosperity, and inclusiveness. It will focus on supporting long-term, multi-stakeholder implementation processes to advance local SDG delivery. Local2030 thus represents a shift in the way the UN engages local stakeholders—one that places individuals, entrepreneurs, local businesses, cities, and local governments as partners in the work of the UN. As such, it is a key means for implementing the UN development system (UNDS) reform on the ground and ensuring that local development is at the core of the revamped UN Country Teams
